svg.aria-label: The same observations on raw and log scales Panel: Raw values Panel: Log values Panel: Same eight observations Original scale $x$; Count Eight observations: [0, 32): 6; [32, 64): 1; [64, 96): 0; [96, 128]: 1 Raw values: 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127. Six of eight values lie below 32. Log scale $z = \log_2(1+x)$; Count Eight observations: [0, 2): 2; [2, 4): 2; [4, 6): 2; [6, 8]: 2 Transformed values are 0 through 7. The largest gaps shrink; these log values are evenly spaced. Same eight observations Raw $x$ | $z$ A: 0 | 0 B: 1 | 1 C: 3 | 2 D: 7 | 3 E: 15 | 4 F: 31 | 5 G: 63 | 6 H: 127 | 7 $z=\log_2(1+x)$ is defined for $x>-1$; every raw value here is nonnegative. Both panels count the same eight samples in different x units. Logs compress this right tail; they do not ensure normality.
